title: Gleaning (Ruth 2)
hookLine: Ruth gathers leftover grain, and Boaz tells his workers to drop some on purpose

lines: LET ME NOW GO TO THE FIELD.
HER HAP WAS TO LIGHT ON BOAZ'S FIELD.
cards: Barley harvest in Bethlehem. Two widows have come home with nothing to eat, and the younger one makes a plan: "Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn."
To glean is to walk behind the reapers and pick up what they drop: stray stalks, the bits at the edges. So Ruth, a foreigner, goes out alone.
And the storyteller says, almost with a wink, "her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz," a relative of Naomi's dead husband.
Then Boaz walks out from town and greets his workers, "The LORD be with you," and they answer, "The LORD bless thee."

teach.h: THE LAW LEFT THE EDGES FOR STRANGERS.
teach.b: Ruth isn't begging. She's using a law. In Leviticus, God tells Israel: "thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest."

Leave them for the poor and the stranger. Deuteronomy adds the forgotten sheaf: don't go back for it; "it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow." Ruth is two of those three at once.
The law built a margin into every farm, so the hungry could feed themselves with their own hands. Boaz notices her. He tells her to stay in his field, and that his young men won't touch her.

teach.h: WHY ME, SEEING I AM A STRANGER?
teach.b: Ruth falls on her face: "Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?"

teach.h: UNDER WHOSE WINGS THOU ART COME.
teach.b: He's heard what she did for Naomi, and he blesses her under the God of Israel, "under whose wings thou art come to trust."

teach.h: LET FALL SOME HANDFULS OF PURPOSE.
teach.b: As she gets up to glean, Boaz quietly tells his reapers: "let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not." The law said leave the edges and what drops.
Boaz goes past it: drop more, on purpose, and say nothing. That evening she beats out what she gathered, and the text says it was about an ephah of barley.
Hearing the name Boaz, the bitter widow from yesterday says, "Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead."

how: Christians read Ruth 2 together with the gleaning laws of Leviticus and Deuteronomy, and some churches and charities name food-rescue work, gathering surplus harvest for people in need, after gleaning.

s: Ruth gleans by begging Boaz for grain
she uses a law that left the edges and the dropped grain for the poor and the stranger.
Boaz tells his reapers to drop extra grain on purpose
"let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her" (Ruth 2:16).
Naomi is angry when she hears Ruth worked in Boaz's field
she says, blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead (Ruth 2:20).

games.q: you're Boaz. a foreign widow is gleaning in your field behind your workers. you've heard how loyal she's been. what do you do?
o: give her a sack of grain in front of everyone.
tell your reapers to drop handfuls for her on purpose, and say nothing.
follow the law, and leave the corners as usual.
games.why: Boaz tells them to let handfuls fall of purpose and to rebuke her not (Ruth 2:16). she finds more than she expected.

practice: Look through the rest of your day for the edges of your field: a little extra time, money, food or attention, the last slice.
Pick one thing you could leave quietly for someone, so they simply find it, the way Ruth found the handfuls: no speech, no credit. If you pray, hold that person in prayer as you decide.

wordCard.voice: Gleaning. Gathering what the reapers leave behind. The law left the edges of the field for the poor and the stranger, and Boaz left more.

orig.note: Hebrew: to glean, to gather up. the verb behind Ruth's gleaning all through Ruth 2.

carryVoice: Your line: drop some on purpose. A kindness that lets someone simply find it. Day seven hundred eight, done.
